evidence.title: CHANGE REQUEST CR-2004-007
evidence.claim: In 2004, adding fillers under vacuum was mandated to prevent pinholes caused by air entrained by micro-silica.
evidence.quote: Reason: pinholes caused by air entrained by micro-silica

evidence.title: LABORATORY TEST REPORT LT-2004-061
evidence.claim: A 2004 lab test confirmed that vacuum deaeration during filler addition eliminates pinholes caused by micro-silica.
evidence.quote: air is entrained by the micro-silica during filler addition and released during curing

evidence.title: Minutes - EF-210 cycle time review, 9 February 2021
evidence.claim: In 2021, a proposal to remove the vacuum step was rejected because micro-silica is required for sag resistance.
evidence.quote: Rejected: micro-silica is needed for sag resistance on ramps and vertical surfaces

evidence.title: CUSTOMER CLAIM CL-2004-003
evidence.claim: In 2004, customer Logistica Fontanili reported pinholes and craters on a floor coated with EF-210, requiring a costly recoating.
evidence.quote: Complaint: pinholes and craters across the floor; recoating required.

evidence.title: Supplier qualification SQ-2010-003 - Quarzi Monterosso S.p.A.
evidence.claim: In 2010, the supplier of quartz flour for EF-210 was changed from Silicati Brenta to Quarzi Monterosso S.p.A.
evidence.quote: Replaces Silicati Brenta paper bags from April 2010.

verdict.process_name: EF-210 epoxy floor coating, Part A
verdict.instruction: Add 500 kg quartz flour (RM-210) and 40 kg micro-silica (RM-212) under vacuum (-0.8 bar).
verdict.reason: The vacuum step was mandated in 2004 to prevent pinholes caused by air entrained by micro-silica (E3, E4), following a customer claim regarding floor defects (E6). Micro-silica remains a required component for sag resistance (E5), and the hazard of air entrainment persists.

chain.claim: Customer reported pinholes and craters on EF-210 floors
Lab tests confirmed micro-silica entrains air released during curing, causing pinholes
Vacuum addition was mandated to eliminate these pinholes

dependencies.name: air entrained by micro-silica
dependencies.note: Micro-silica is still used for sag resistance
